added_lines: 25th october 2026 30th sunday in ordinary time all you need is love first of all i want to say a sincere ‘thank you’ to all those who took the trouble this past week to respond to my invitation to share any suggestions you had with regard to the enhancing of our lives as a community here at mount argus. let me assure you that all your suggestions are valued and are already forming part of our ongoing agenda in planning the way forward. not surprisingly, there was considerable reference to things that were valued in the past, but b ecause of covid, change of personnel, and other factors, were no longer in operation. many of these were lay-led, and many related to helping people deepen their knowledge of their faith and their prayer life. without in any way wishing to attempt to turn back the clock, as it were, there i s still very much a need for such projects. it would be very much my hope that before christmas – only two months away – we might have a general meeting to discuss the way forward. as has been frequently pointed out in recent years, we cannot si mply continue as if nothing has changed – either here, or in the wider church, or in the world i n general. to take but a simple and obvious example – the vast majority of the liturgical celebra tions in our church are led by men in their eighties. for the bulk of those celebrations we are attempting to light and heat an area that is less than one twentieth occupied – surely not in keeping with care for i, and i’m sure each of you, could list many other areas where present practise is not sustai nable. but i say all this, not in despair, but in the hope that we can mu ster together all the good will, all the talents, all the commitment that i know, without being in any patronising, exist in our community – but we so often take for granted, and don’t allow o r encourage to flourish. and our gospel today is reminding us of the need to constantly be aware of the essentials at the heart of being are tricky questions – this time it’s “which is the greatest comm andment of the law?” and you’ll remember jesus’ reply – about loving god totally, and loving our neighbour as ourselves. “on these two commandments hang the whole law, and the prophets also.” and i think it’s good to bring ourselves back to this passa ge frequently, especially at those times when we can easily get confused – what is the teaching of the church about this or that; how do i apply the teaching of christ to this situation? and the answer always is – do the loving thing – are we showing our love for god, and for our neighbour, by behaving in this way? jesus is reminding us that all he is asking of us is that we should do all those relatively rou tine and minor things in a loving and positive way. no need for us to do anything earth-shattering!
